notes: Left-hand of the two vertical strip drawings on printed page 233 (IA leaf n244; IIIF image _0245; crop x0–905 of the page). Block-by-block perspective line drawing with printed house numbers on the curb line: 1702, 1712, 1720, 1726, 1730, 1736, '18th St.', 1800 (Glessner, with its arched entry and 18th-Street wall), 1808, 1812. Shows uniform setbacks, front lawns, a continuous line of curbside posts/lamp-or-hitching posts and street trees, a carriage in the roadway. Drawn c.1892–93: 1702 here is the pre-Glessner-Lee-townhouse house (pa-1702-43, demolished before 1904) and 1726 is the early house later replaced, so for 1904 this is evidence of the earlier generation at those two lots; 1720, 1736, 1800–1812 are the buildings standing in 1904. Diagrammatic — façades are simplified and proportions not reliable for measurement; treat as a numbered sequence/massing guide.

notes: Right-hand strip on printed page 233 (IA leaf n244; crop x895–1820). Printed numbers 1701 (Hibbard), 1709, 1721 (Dexter), 1729 (Pullman, with the long 18th-Street frontage, conservatory/grounds behind), '18th St.', 1801 (Kimball, turreted château), 1811, 1815. Street trees, curbside posts and fences along the east side; 18th Street shown running east toward the lake. 1709 is labelled but the drawing is too schematic to say whether it shows the Williams house or its Burnham & Root successor (Palmer Kellogg) — building_id given for the successor as the likelier 1892–93 occupant; verify. Same limits as the companion strip: a diagram, not a measured view.

notes: Companion text to the four strip drawings. p. 232: drive turns off Michigan Boulevard 'and reach by Sixteenth Street — Prairie Avenue, a neighborhood of millionaires'; names Pullman 1729, Field 1905, Pike 2101. p. 234: Pullman residence description (remodelled 1892 with picture gallery and palm-house; conservatory and lawn on the south side of 18th St. toward Calumet; the Fort Dearborn massacre cottonwood and the Massacre Monument at the foot of 18th St.); 'From Eighteenth to Twenty-second' (Doane 1827). pp. 267–270: house-number-by-house-number list of 'South Side residents — Prairie Avenue' (e.g. 1936 S. W. Allerton; 2009 Mrs Sarah Meyer; 2013 W. H. Reid; 2100 J. B. Sherman; 2115 P. D. Armour; 2126 C. D. Hamill; 2130 Thomas Murdoch; 2140 Byron L. Smith) — useful to key the drawings to occupants c.1893. Page 229 carries a 'Route of South Side Drive' sketch map (Michigan Blvd → 16th St → Prairie Ave → south). Index lines quoted from IA OCR.
